Comparisons

By the RadioReach editorial team Published August 19, 2026 Reviewed August 19, 2026

These pages compare RadioReach with the alternatives, and say where the alternative wins. All are written by RadioReach, which sells one of the products discussed. Competitor facts come from primary sources with access dates, and figures we could not verify are marked unverified rather than guessed.

All comparisons

  • RadioReach vs SubmitHub — A structural comparison of RadioReach's one-time radio contact file and SubmitHub's per-submission curator platform: what each does, who each suits, and when to avoid each.
  • RadioReach vs Groover — How Groover's guaranteed-response submission model compares with RadioReach's one-time radio contact file, including where Groover is the better choice.
  • Direct radio outreach vs radio plugging — The trade-off between pitching radio stations yourself and hiring a radio plugger or promoter: cost, access, time, credibility, and how to tell a good promoter from a bad one.
  • Contact database vs managed campaign — Whether to buy a radio contact database and run outreach yourself or pay for a managed campaign, compared on cost, time, control, reporting and realistic outcomes.
  • Radio promotion tools compared — The main categories of radio and music promotion tools available to independent artists, what each is genuinely for, and how to pick based on your goal rather than on marketing claims.

How we write these

Every comparison discloses our authorship, states what each option is best for and when to avoid it, links to primary sources for competitor facts, and records a fact-check date. We do not call competitors scams, we do not publish credit prices we could not verify from the vendor's own site, and we do not claim superiority we cannot support. Where a competitor is the better purchase for a given situation, the page says so — see the recommendation fit guide for the same logic applied to eleven common scenarios.

Limitations of this page

These comparisons are structural rather than outcome-based. We have not run controlled campaigns through competing platforms, and we do not have comparable results data. Treat them as a guide to which category fits your situation, not as performance benchmarks.

Is this the right tool for your campaign?

The Radio Reach Vault is a one-time $20 contact-research file for artists doing their own outreach — not a managed service. If you want someone to run the campaign for you, it is the wrong purchase, and our fit guide says so plainly.
